NAAD0* is a medical classification code used within the Danish healthcare system to denote an epidural block. In the context of the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) and its 2024 reporting, this code plays a specific role in tracking and evaluating clinical practices. Specifically, NAAD0* is utilized alongside other codes, such as BABZ00 (insertion of an epidural catheter), to determine whether an epidural was used in a patient's treatment [^src1]. This data collection is directly tied to the measurement of [[epidural-use]] in acute surgical care [^src1].

The use of NAAD0* represents a strategic methodological adjustment in how quality indicators are calculated. According to the 2024 AKDB report, the code is now collected directly from the National Patient Registry (LPR) to calculate Indicator 9 [^src1]. This shift in data sourcing was implemented to optimize the underlying data basis for the indicator, ensuring more accurate and standardized tracking of epidural interventions. This technical change is part of a broader narrative of quality development in acute surgery in Denmark, which relies on continuous database operations, risk adjustment, and standardized indicators to improve treatment standards.
